title: With no income, a $15,000 buffer covers about 4 to 6 months for a single adult depending on the city
question: If I arrive with savings and no income yet, how many months could I cover housing and everyday costs in each place?
dek: A transparent scenario: sourced asking rent plus Market Basket Measure non-shelter costs, scaled to household size. Change the assumptions to match your situation.

findings.headline: A single adult with $15,000 and no income lasts about 5.9 months in Sherbrooke but 4.0 in Vancouver
findings.detail: Scenario, not a prediction: monthly cost = 2026-Q2 average asking rent for a 1-bedroom apartment + the MBM non-shelter basket (food, clothing, transportation, communication, other) for one person (reference cost x sqrt(1/reference household size), divided by 12). Longest runway: Sherbrooke 5.9, Québec City 5.5, Regina 5.5, Saint John 5.4; shortest: Vancouver 4.0, Toronto 4.2, Victoria 4.2, Halifax 4.4 months. Median 5.0 months. Excluded: one-off costs (flights, deposits, furniture), taxes, benefits, income, health costs and any shelter cost beyond rent.

stat.label: median months of runway, single adult, $15,000

findings.calc: months = 15,000 / (asking rent 1BR + (MBM total - MBM shelter) x sqrt(1/referenceHouseholdSize) / 12); MBM = observation-year current dollars, 2023 base, reference household of four (five in Nunavut); rent = REF_DATE 2026-04.

findings.headline: A couple with a child and $25,000 lasts about 6.4 months in Sherbrooke but 4.4 in Vancouver
findings.detail: Scenario: 2-bedroom asking rent + MBM non-shelter costs scaled to 3 persons (x sqrt(3/referenceHouseholdSize) = 87%). Longest runway: Sherbrooke 6.4, Québec City 6.2, Regina 6.1, Moncton 6.0; shortest: Vancouver 4.4, Toronto 4.8, Victoria 4.8, Halifax 5.0 months (median 5.6). Rent is 42% of the median monthly outlay, so rent differences between cities drive most of the spread.

stat.label: median months of runway, couple + child, $25,000

findings.calc: months = 25,000 / (asking rent 2BR + (MBM total - MBM shelter) x sqrt(3/referenceHouseholdSize) / 12).

findings.headline: Rent is 41% to 60% of the single-adult monthly outlay; the non-rent basket is far more similar between cities
findings.detail: Non-shelter MBM costs for one person range from $1,446 to $1,573 a month across these places (London and Kitchener–Waterloo lowest, Fredericton highest), whereas 1-bedroom asking rent spans $1,040 to $2,280. The MBM is a modest-basket benchmark, not an individual's actual spending.

stat.label: median share of monthly outlay that is rent (single adult)

findings.calc: rent / (rent + (MBM total - MBM shelter) x sqrt(1/referenceHouseholdSize) / 12) for each place; non-shelter = total - shelter (includes food, clothing, transportation, communication, other).

charts.notes: Modeled scenario using regional MBM baskets, not a ranking of measured city living costs. Excludes one-off costs, tax, benefits and income. MBM 2025; rent 2026-Q2.

charts.title: Months of runway by household type
charts.subtitle: Single adult ($15,000, 1BR) vs couple + 1 child ($25,000, 2BR)
charts.notes: Scenario only. Savings buffers are stated assumptions, not typical values.

interpretation: Use this as a stress test of how quickly savings run down, not a forecast. Because rent is the biggest and most variable piece, the same savings buy more months in lower-rent places - but job prospects and wages differ too (see the work pages).
Real first-months spending usually also includes a rental deposit or first/last month, furnishing, winter clothing and transport to settle in; these are left out here and would shorten the runway.
methodology: Monthly cost = latest average asking rent for the stated apartment size (StatCan 46-10-0092-01) + non-shelter MBM costs / 12.

Non-shelter MBM = Total threshold - Shelter component (Food, Clothing, Transportation, Communication services, Other expenses) from StatCan 11-10-0066-01, 2023-base MBM, observation-year current dollars, for the MBM region mapped to each place; this is the reference household of four (five in Nunavut).

Household scaling uses StatCan's square-root equivalence scale: cost for n persons = reference-family cost x sqrt(n/referenceHouseholdSize) (1 person 50%, 3 persons 87%). We verified it reproduces the published family-size totals in table 11-10-0104-01 (Toronto 2025: 1 person 31,440; 2 persons 44,463; 3 persons 54,456).

Months of runway = stated savings / monthly cost. Stated savings are $15,000 (single) and $25,000 (couple + 1 child). No income, no taxes, no benefits, no one-off costs, no inflation between 2025 (MBM) and the rent quarter.
limitations: MBM regions differ from the CMAs and several places share one regional value (e.g. Victoria, Kelowna and Abbotsford-Mission all use 'British Columbia, population 100,000 to 499,999'); Gatineau's mapping to the Quebec 100,000-499,999 class is an assumption.

The MBM is a modest-basket benchmark for a reference family, scaled by an equivalence scale; it is not a measure of what an individual newcomer spends, and it uses the basket observation year while rent uses its stated quarter.
Asking rents are averages of advertised apartments; the cheapest listings may be smaller or in less central areas.
Coverage: places not in the StatCan rent table (Charlottetown, Brandon, Whitehorse, Yellowknife, Iqaluit) are excluded.
